claim: Saretto (Nov 2005 WP; precursor of Goyal-Saretto 2009), OptionMetrics Jan 1996-Jun 2005, ATM options with 30-60 days to expiry (avg ~47 days, moneyness 0.95-1.05), bought at month start at bid-ask mid and held to month end, unhedged: long-short (decile 10 minus 1) equal-weighted straddle portfolio on cross-sectional forecast of change in log ATM IV averaged 12.9%/month (monthly Sharpe 0.977), before explicit spread costs; decile 10 straddles averaged +5.6%/month, decile 1 -7.2%.
quote: Portfolio 10, which corresponds to stocks with large predicted increase in volatility, has average returns equal to 8.8%, 5.6%, and 5.6% for calls, puts, and straddles, respectively.
title: Saretto (2005 working paper) Option Returns and the Cross-Sectional Predictability of Implied Volatility

claim: Saretto (2005 WP), same sample/setup (1996-Jun 2005, 30-60 day ATM options, 1-month hold, unhedged straddles/calls/puts): the signal is low ATM IV relative to cross-sectional average and relative to the stock's own 12-month average of IV and of realised vol (regression of change in log IV on iv, iv minus 12m avg IV, iv minus 12m avg RV). Straddle returns persist after controlling for transaction costs and liquidity: up to 8.8%/month.
quote: After controlling for transaction costs and liquidity characteristics of the options the average monthly return to expiration of the straddles portfolio is as high as 8.8% with a monthly Sharpe ratio of 0.271.
title: Saretto (2005 working paper) Option Returns and the Cross-Sectional Predictability of Implied Volatility

claim: Saretto (2005 WP): sample ends 2005 (before 2015). Long-short results are fragile to timing: skipping the first trading day of the month cuts the straddle long-short return from 12.9% to 11.6%/month; replacing market IV with the model forecast removes the profit (consistent with the signal being a better vol forecast).
quote: The profitability of the trading strategy completely disappears suggesting that the modified price obtained from the volatility forecast is closer to the 'true' price of the option.
title: Saretto (2005 working paper) Option Returns and the Cross-Sectional Predictability of Implied Volatility

claim: Saretto (2005 WP): the long-short straddle return is positive in both rising and falling VIX months but larger when VIX rises (17.6% vs 8.5%/month); stock-characteristic double sorts leave quintile long-short straddle returns of 6.9% to 12.8%/month, larger for small, high book-to-market, past-loser stocks (sample Jan 1996-Jun 2005, 30-60 day ATM straddles, unhedged).
quote: The long-short portfolio strategy has statistically significant average returns that range from 6.9% to 12.8% per month
title: Saretto (2005 working paper) Option Returns and the Cross-Sectional Predictability of Implied Volatility

claim: Cao, Vasquez, Xiao, Zhan (Quarterly Journal of Finance 2023): delta-hedged equity option returns fall with volatility of volatility (VOV, std of daily % change in vol over prior month; implied vol from 30-day options, EGARCH(1,1) vol on rolling 252 days, intraday 5-min realised vol). Quintile portfolios of delta-neutral written calls (daily rebalanced) sorted on VOV earn top-minus-bottom spreads of 0.52% to 1.04% per month. This is a hedged result for the option WRITER, not a buyer's return; sample period, maturity and costs not read (pages 1-8 only).
quote: The return spreads between the top and bottom quintiles are statistically significant for the three VOV measures ranging from 0.52% to 1.04% per month.
title: Why Does Volatility Uncertainty Predict Equity Option Returns?

claim: Cao, Vasquez, Xiao, Zhan (2023): the implied-VOV effect is driven by upward vol changes (VOV+) and the idiosyncratic component of IV changes; authors attribute it to model risk and gambling demand, so low-VOV stocks have higher delta-hedged option returns for buyers of hedged positions.
quote: we find that the idiosyncratic-VOV is the driving component for the negative relation between implied VOV and option returns.
title: Why Does Volatility Uncertainty Predict Equity Option Returns?

claim: Vasquez (JFQA, 2017): ranking firms on slope of the implied volatility term structure, straddle portfolios with high slope outperform low-slope ones; not explained by traditional factors or jump risk. Sample period, maturity, holding period, effect size and costs NOT read (only abstract cached).
quote: Straddle portfolios with high slopes of the volatility term structure outperform straddle portfolios with low slopes by an economically and statistically significant amount.
title: Equity Volatility Term Structures and the Cross-Section of Option Returns

claim: An, Ang, Bali, Cakici (NBER WP 19590, Oct 2013; JF 2014): context only, outcome is STOCK returns not option returns: stocks with large 1-month increases in call IV have high next-month stock returns; sorted deciles spread about 1%/month, persists to six months.
quote: Sorting stocks ranked into decile portfolios by past call implied volatilities produces spreads in average returns of approximately 1% per month
title: The Joint Cross Section of Stocks and Options
